t.6.65.1: Hearing that Nikumbha had been slain and that Kumbha too had been struck down, Rāvaṇa, utterly beside himself with fury, blazed up like fire.
t.6.65.2: But the Nairṛta, stupefied by the two together, wrath and grief, urged on the large-eyed Makarākṣa, son of Khara.
t.6.65.3: Go, son, commanded by me and accompanied by an army, and slay Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa, those two, together with the forest-dwellers.
t.6.65.4: Hearing Rāvaṇa's words, the heroic and proud son of Khara, the bold night-roamer Makarākṣa, said, "So be it."
t.6.65.5: Having saluted Daśagrīva and also having circumambulated him, the mighty one went forth from the gleaming palace at Rāvaṇa's command.
t.6.65.6: Khara's son spoke these words to the commander of the army who stood nearby: "Let my chariot be brought quickly, and let the army be brought with haste."
t.6.65.7: Hearing those words of his, the night-roaming commander of the army brought the chariot and the army as well into his presence.
t.6.65.8: Having circumambulated the chariot, keeping it to his right, the night-roamer mounted it and urged on the charioteer: "Bring my chariot forward quickly!"
t.6.65.9: Then Makarākṣa spoke these words to all those rākṣasas: "O rākṣasas, all of you, fight in front of me!"
t.6.65.10: I have been commanded by Rāvaṇa, the great-souled king of the rākṣasas, to slay in battle both of them, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.65.11: O night-rangers, today with my finest arrows I shall slay Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva the monkey, and the other vānaras as well.
t.6.65.12: Today, with the blows of my spear, I shall burn up the great army of the monkeys that has arrived here, as fire consumes dry firewood.
t.6.65.13: Having heard those words of Makarākṣa, all those night-rangers, mighty, equipped with various weapons and fully prepared, stood ready.
t.6.65.14: Those heroes, able to take any form at will, fanged and tawny-eyed, roared like elephants, terrifying, with their hair dishevelled.
t.6.65.15: Then, surrounding the huge-bodied son of Khara, the huge-bodied ones advanced in delight, making the earth tremble.
t.6.65.16: Then, from the thousands of conches and kettledrums struck on every side, and from the roars and the slapping of arms, there arose a mighty sound.
t.6.65.17: Then the goad slipped from the hand of his charioteer, and at that moment the banner of that rākṣasa also suddenly fell down.
t.6.65.18: His horses yoked to the chariot, bereft of their vigour, moved on with faltering feet and went forward dejected, their faces wet with tears.
t.6.65.19: At the departure of that fierce, evil-minded Makarākṣa, a harsh and dreadful wind blew upon him, laden with dust.
t.6.65.20: Having seen those omens, the rākṣasas, most mighty in valour, all went forth without heeding them, to where Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa stood.
t.6.65.21: Those night-rangers, skilled in warfare, their complexions like clouds, elephants and the bodies of buffaloes, who had many times been pierced by maces and swords at the forefront of battles, roamed about on every side, roaring and crying, “I first! I first!”
